::: {#sol-residual-grad}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
residual_grad = first_layer_grad(make_deep(residual=True))
print(residual_grad, plain_grad)
```

The [gradient](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient) has size `r sprintf("%.1e", py$residual_grad)`,
against `r sprintf("%.1e", py$plain_grad)` without [residual connections](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/backpropagation.html#def-residual-connection).
A block computes $\vhidval + f(\vhidval)$,
so its derivative with respect to $\vhidval$ is the identity matrix plus the derivative of $f$.
Going back through a block,
the gradient keeps a copy of itself through the identity,
however small the derivative of $f$ is.
Without the [residual connection](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/backpropagation.html#def-residual-connection),
the gradient passes only through the derivative of $f$,
and shrinks when that derivative is small.

:::
